_comment: THE FIRST BATCH. Real LEDGER content, not a demo image: the signage the
street already asks for and renders as blank coloured panels today.
WorldBuilder.NeonSigns carries eight (placeId, colour, word) rows and draws
an emissive cube; Dressing.HasFascia decides which premises carry a
signboard band and what sits on it is a tinted plate. Every `sign_*` word
below is copied EXACTLY from the NeonSigns table so the output can be bound
to an existing call site rather than to a folder nobody reads.
SETTING, and it is not negotiable: Meridian is a British port town in the
LATE-ANALOG eighties and nineties. Landlines, cash, paper. Not the 1950s.
SCHEMA 2, 25 Aug 2026, WRITTEN OFF THE FIRST REAL RUN. Jafar generated all
twelve on an RX 6700 over Vulkan - 12 written, 0 failed, ~20 minutes, no
blanks. Four of the twelve came back wrong and the two faults were both
ours, not the model's:
1. THERE WAS NO NEGATIVE-PROMPT CHANNEL. Every exclusion we wrote - `no
signage legible`, `no perspective`, `no people, no cars` - went into
the POSITIVE prompt, where a diffusion model reads the nouns and draws
them. `wall_soot_brick` came back as a photographic street corner with
a crisp white sign board on it reading WEORED S HONJ. See `negatives`
below, and read the cfg note there before believing the channel acts.
2. TWO PROMPTS ASKED FOR SOMETHING NO IMAGE MODEL DOES. Dense small print
and typewriter table cells come back as gibberish letterforms in every
current diffusion model, including the named next rung. Short lines
are already excellent: STEAM LAUNDRY, THE HARBOUR LIGHTS / PLUS
SUPPORT / FRIDAY 8PM / ADMISSION 2 POUNDS all came back correctly
spelled and period-true. So the two body-text prompts now ask for the
RULED STRUCTURE, which is what the eye reads at street distance.
EVERY ITEM CARRIES ITS SEED EXPLICITLY, and that is a fix rather than a
decoration. The seed used to be `seed_base + position in this list`, so
inserting one item silently re-seeded every item after it - and the resume
rule (regenerate when the recipe changed, skip when it did not) would then
regenerate the whole batch for an edit that touched one line. The seeds
below are the ones his successful run actually used.
THESE RIDE IN EVERY PROMPT. They are data, not documentation, so an
editor adding a thirteenth item cannot forget them: the renderer appends
`rules_clause` to every positive prompt and refuses to build a prompt
that does not carry it (imagegen.py: build_prompt / _selftest_rules).
WHY: every 1980s British advert, poster and packet is still in copyright
for decades yet, and trade mark was the ONLY claim Getty actually won in
[2025] EWHC 2863 (Ch). A model asked for `a British high street in 1989`
will happily paint a real brewery's livery on a pub. So we never ask for
one. In-world brands only, which is better content anyway - MICKEY'S is
a place in this game and a real brewery is not.
AND THIS IS THE ONE CLAUSE THAT STAYS IN THE POSITIVE PROMPT, 25 Aug.
Every other exclusion moved to `negatives` below. This one did not, and
the reason is measured rather than cautious: sd-cli only evaluates the
unconditional branch when cfg != 1.0 (see `negatives._comment`), and this
batch runs at cfg 1.0 because Z-Image-Turbo is distilled for it. A
negative prompt is therefore INERT here - so moving the anti-brand,
anti-real-person clause into it would have deleted the only instruction
the model actually receives on the subject. It is mirrored into the
negative as well, where it will start acting the day an item raises cfg.
The exclusion scan in imagegen.py exempts this clause BY NAME and prints
that it did, so the hole is a line of output rather than a silence.
content_rules.rules_clause: invented fictional shop name only, no real company names, no real brand logos, no trade marks, no real person, no recognisable faces, no celebrity likeness

_comment: One shared style block so twelve prompts do not drift into twelve looks.
The reference is game-design/reference/ (GTA V frames, Jafar's, internal
comparison only) read for what a lettered street does, not copied.
`no people, no cars` USED TO BE IN THE SUFFIX and rode into all twelve
positive prompts. It is now `deserted, empty street` - the same intent
said as a thing to draw rather than a thing to omit - and the omission
half moved to `negatives.default`. This DOES change the positive prompt
of every item, so the resume rule regenerates all twelve on the next run;
that is deliberate and it is why the run publishes whatever is already on
disk BEFORE it generates anything (imagegen.py: Publisher.publish_existing).
The images he picked out are in git before the first pixel is redrawn.
`by_kind` overrides the whole prefix and/or suffix for one kind. A wall
texture is not a photograph of a street and must not be asked for as one:
the word `photograph` is exactly what produced a coping, a corner and a
pavement in a frame that was supposed to be nothing but brick.
style.prefix: photograph, straight-on flat elevation, evenly lit,
style.suffix: British port town, late 1980s, overcast North Sea daylight, damp salt-weathered paintwork, soot and grime, deserted empty street, sharp legible lettering, period-correct signwriting

wall.prefix: flat orthographic texture sheet, square-on to the surface, uniform even lighting, the surface filling the frame edge to edge,
wall.suffix: British port town, late 1980s, damp salt-weathered masonry, soot and grime, uniform weathering across the whole frame, seamless tileable material sample, single continuous surface

_comment: THE NEGATIVE CHANNEL, added 25 Aug. Composed as default + by_kind[kind] +
item.negative and passed to sd-cli as --negative-prompt.
THE FLAG IS VERIFIED FROM THE SHIPPED BINARY, not from a doc example.
`sd-cli.exe` out of sd-master-97d2990-bin-win-vulkan-x64.zip (38,784,820
bytes, the size pinned in imagegen.py) has `--negative-prompt` in its
string table followed by its own help text, `the negative prompt
(default: "")`, in the same table as --prompt, --cfg-scale, --steps and
every other long flag this pipeline already passes successfully.
AND THE PART THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE FLAG: A NEGATIVE PROMPT DOES
NOTHING AT cfg 1.0. stable-diffusion.cpp's `resolve_guidance` sets
`use_uncond` only when `img_cfg != txt_cfg`; for a model with no image
conditioning img_cfg is forced to 1.0, so `--cfg-scale 1.0` means the
unconditional branch is never evaluated and the negative prompt is never
encoded. Z-Image-Turbo is distilled for cfg 1.0 (the project's own doc
page uses 1.0 for Turbo and 5.0 for Base), which is why this batch runs
there. So: the channel exists, it is wired end to end, and on the twelve
shipped items it is RECORDED AND INERT - the manifest says so per image
and the run summary counts both populations. The fix that actually
removed the sign from the brick wall is the positive prompt no longer
naming one.
The two `probe_*` items at the bottom are the measurement that decides
whether cfg > 1 is usable on this distilled model: same prompt, same
seed, same size, cfg 1.0 against cfg 2.0. Nothing else in this file
raises cfg, because a number nobody has measured is not a setting.
A NEGATIVE PROMPT IS A LIST OF NOUNS, NOT A SENTENCE OF REFUSALS.
Writing `no people` in the negative asks for `no people` to be pushed
away, which is not the same as pushing `people` away. imagegen.py's
validator refuses a negative containing `no `/`without`, and its
rejecting case is exactly that.
negatives.default: watermark, signature, artist signature, modern sans-serif typeface, helvetica, arial, modern digital typography, oversaturated, hdr, colour cast, colourful, people, person, crowd, pedestrians, face, hands, cars, vehicles, traffic, bicycle, mobile phone, computer screen, plastic modern fittings, real company logo, real brand, trade mark, celebrity, recognisable face

_note: WHAT THE MODEL CAN AND CANNOT DO, measured on the 25 Aug run and not
assumed: the two headline lines came back PERFECT - correct spelling,
period-correct condensed capitals. The clause that asked for `smaller
regulation clauses in dense small print` came back as gibberish
letterforms, because no current diffusion model renders a paragraph of
legible body copy - and the named next rung (FLUX.1-schnell) fails the
same way, so a bigger download is not the fix.
So this asks for the STRUCTURE instead: a ruled panel, printed rules,
an even grey block of type. At the two metres a player ever sees it
from, that is exactly what a dock notice reads as.
DO NOT RE-ADD THE SMALL PRINT. Jafar, 25 Aug, on the small text: `maybe

_seen: OPENED 26 Aug. THE TITLE IS PERFECT AND EVERY ROW BELOW IT IS NOISE:
`MERIDIAN FERRY` is flawless signwriting and the twenty-odd timetable
rows are illegible glyph-shaped marks. That is Jafar's own reading of
the first batch - `text is good on some and bad on other, esp. small
text` - reproducing exactly, so it is a property of the model at this
size and not a bad seed.
AND IT IS A PHOTOGRAPH OF A SIGN IN A STREET: post, pavement, kerb,
shopfronts behind, sky, depth of field. `negatives.by_kind.notice`
names every one of those nouns - and is INERT at cfg 1.0, so it has
never been read. The two faults this kind has are the two the
negative was written to prevent.
THE FIX FOR SMALL TEXT IS NOT A BETTER PROMPT. Ask for a notice whose
content is BLOCKS rather than lines - a ruled grid, a dense paragraph
read as texture - or generate the board empty and set the timetable as
real type over it, which is the only way rows a player can read will
ever happen. Decide before the big batch: twenty illegible timetables
cost the same as twenty good ones.
_note: SAME MEASUREMENT AS THE DOCK NOTICE. The heading came back perfect and
`a column of departure times in typewriter figures` came back as
nonsense strings in the cells. A timetable is read as a GRID, so the
grid is what is asked for: ruled columns, horizontal rules, short even
rows of figures. Digit-shaped glyphs that do not spell a real time are
fine at street distance in a way that gibberish WORDS are not - that
is the whole reason this one keeps figures and the dock notice does
not keep clauses.
DO NOT ASK FOR READABLE TIMES.

_note: THE WORST IMAGE OF THE FIRST RUN AND THE ONE THAT PROVED FAULT 1. The
old prompt said `ghost of a painted sign almost gone, no signage
legible, evenly lit, no perspective` and what came back was a
photographic street corner - coping, corner, pavement - carrying a
crisp white sign board reading WEORED S HONJ. Every noun it was told
not to draw, it drew.
Three changes, and only the first is the negative channel:
1. every exclusion moved to `negatives.by_kind.wall` - AND THE
PROBES BELOW SHOW THIS ONE DID NOTHING. This item runs at cfg
1.0, where sd-cli never evaluates the unconditional branch, so
its negatives have never been read. `probe_wall_cfg1` carries
this exact positive prompt at cfg 1.0 and came back with no sign
at all. The move is still right - it is what makes the exclusions
live the moment cfg moves - but 2 and 3 are what fixed this;
2. `photograph` replaced by `flat orthographic texture sheet` for
this kind - the word was asking for a photographed scene, and it
got one;
3. THE GHOST SIGN IS GONE FROM THE TEXTURE ON PURPOSE. A faded
painted sign is good Meridian content and it is a DECAL, not a
tiling wall: baking one into the surface both breaks the tile and
puts the word `sign` in the prompt for a picture whose whole
requirement is that there is no sign in it. If we want ghost
signs, they are their own item on the next batch.
The brickwork itself was genuinely good and that description is kept
word for word.

_seen: OPENED 26 Aug, THE FIRST TIME ANY OF THESE REACHED THE REPOSITORY,
AND IT HAS TWO FAULTS NEITHER OF WHICH ANY NUMBER LOOKED FOR:
1. A WHITE BORDER AROUND THE WHOLE IMAGE. It is a framed picture of
a wall, not a wall. A tiling surface with a border tiles a GRID
of white lines across every building in the district, which is
the most visible possible failure and the blank check cannot see
it: spread reads 242/255, healthy, because a border is a small
fraction of the pixels and the middle is fine.
2. IT IS METAL, NOT RENDER. Panel joints with rusted bolt heads at
every corner - that is riveted cladding. The prompt asked for
painted render blistered back to grey render beneath, and the
peeling and the salt bloom did arrive; the substrate did not.
BOTH ARE FIXES FOR THE NEXT BATCH AND NEITHER IS A PROMPT TWEAK ALONE:
a tiling surface needs a tiling CHECK (compare the edge rows against
the opposite edge - a seam and a border both show there), which is a
measurement this tool does not have and should, because `spread`
answers `is the picture blank` and nothing answers `does it tile`.

items.binds_to: MEASUREMENT ONLY - not shipped, not bound to anything. The A side.
_note: THE A/B THAT DECIDES WHETHER THE NEGATIVE CHANNEL IS EVER USABLE HERE.
Same prompt, same seed, same size as its twin below; the ONLY
difference is cfg, and cfg is the switch that decides whether sd-cli
evaluates the negative prompt at all. 512x512 keeps both sides cheap
(~70s and ~140s on the RX 6700 by the measured rate) and keeps them on
the same VAE flag path, so the comparison is of one variable.
READ THEM SIDE BY SIDE: if B is burnt, over-contrasted or mangled, the
answer is that this distilled model cannot take cfg > 1 and the
negative channel stays inert until the model changes - which is a
finding, not a failure. If B is clean, negatives become usable and the
wall items should raise cfg.
READ 26 Aug, BOTH SIDES, AND THE ANSWER IS NOT THE ONE THE LINE ABOVE
EXPECTED. B is NOT burnt: it is a clean brick wall with more contrast,
brighter mortar and more salt bloom than A. So this distilled model
DOES take cfg 2.0 and the negative channel is usable - that half is
settled.
But A is clean too, and A is the case that decides. A runs at cfg 1.0,
where sd-cli never evaluates the unconditional branch, so its negative
prompt was NEVER READ - and A carries the same positive prompt, word
for word, as `wall_soot_brick`, the item that came back with a crisp
sign board reading WEORED S HONJ. Neither probe has any sign in it.
THEREFORE CHANGE 1 - moving every exclusion into the negatives - IS
NOT WHAT REMOVED THE SIGN. Changes 2 and 3 did it alone: dropping the
word `photograph`, and taking the word `sign` out of a picture whose
whole requirement is that there is no sign in it. The negative channel
was credited with a fix it could not have made, because it never ran.
COST, from the run: 34s for A against 63s for B, 1.85x - close to the
2x two model evaluations per step predicts, and measured rather than
assumed. We are NOT paying it: the wall items stay at cfg 1.0.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE, and it is stated because a probe is 512x512
with seed 8041 and the item it stands for is 1024x1024 with seed 8036:
one sample each, and a clean 512 does not prove a clean 1024. It
proves the negatives were not load-bearing on the fault they were
credited with.
AND THAT LAST SENTENCE IS FALSE. IT WAS WRITTEN THE SAME MORNING, OFF
THESE TWO PROBES, AND THE 1024 WALL LANDED IN THE REPOSITORY HOURS
LATER WITH A SIGN ON IT: `wall_soot_brick.png` carries `Rao Hiau` in
white on a dark brick, top right. So the fault the negatives were
credited with never went away, and the paragraph above is kept only
because the mistake in it is the useful part.
THE MISTAKE IS RULE 5b's, AIMED AT A PROBE. A guard must be tested on
the case it should PASS; a PROBE must be run on a case where the fault
actually OCCURS. Neither 512 probe had a sign on it — not the cfg 2.0
one and not the cfg 1.0 one — so neither could say anything about what
removes a sign. I read `both clean` as `the negative is unnecessary`
when the only honest reading is `this probe did not reproduce the
fault, so it measured nothing about the fault`. The caveat directly
above says a probe may not transfer, and I quoted it and concluded
past it in the same breath.
WHAT IS ACTUALLY KNOWN, kept narrow on purpose. Both probes ran at the
same size and seed and differed only in cfg, and the model takes cfg
2.0 without burning — that half stands. The sign appears at 1024/seed
8036 and not at 512/seed 8041, with the negative INERT in both, so
size or seed moves it and the negative has never once been tested
against a frame that had the fault. The untried experiment is cfg 2.0
AT 1024 ON SEED 8036 — the same picture that failed, with the negative
channel live — and until that runs, nothing here says whether the
negatives help.
